record.original_question: Develop a theory of signed Hoffman graphs analogous to the Hoffman graph machinery used for unsigned graphs.

evidence.quote: Woo and Neumaier [80] introduced the notion of Hoffman graphs, which has proved an essential tool in many results involving the smallest eigenvalue of unsigned graphs (see [59]). Perhaps a theory of signed Hoffman graphs is possible as well.
Problem 3.17. Extend the theory of Hoffman graphs to signed graphs.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A signed graph is a pair $(G,\sigma)$ where $G=(V,E)$ is a finite simple graph and $\sigma:E\to\{+1,-1\}$ is a sign function on the edges. The adjacency matrix $A(G,\sigma)$ is the $V\times V$ matrix whose $(u,v)$-entry is $\sigma(uv)$ if $uv\in E$ and $0$ otherwise; its smallest eigenvalue $\lambda_{\min}(G,\sigma)$ is a basic spectral invariant.

For unsigned graphs, a Hoffman graph is a triple $\mathfrak h=(H,\mu)$ where $H$ is an undirected graph with vertex set partitioned into a set of "slim" vertices $V_s(\mathfrak h)$ and a set of "fat" vertices $V_f(\mathfrak h)$, such that every fat vertex is adjacent only to slim vertices and no two fat vertices share a slim neighbour. The special matrix of $\mathfrak h$ is $A(\mathfrak h)=A_s-N N^{\top}$, where $A_s$ is the adjacency matrix of the slim subgraph and $N$ is the slim–fat incidence matrix; the smallest eigenvalue of $\mathfrak h$ is $\lambda_{\min}(\mathfrak h):=\lambda_{\min}(A(\mathfrak h))$. One says that an (unsigned) graph $G$ is represented by a family $\mathcal F$ of Hoffman graphs if $G$ admits an "$\mathcal F$-decomposition"; this machinery yields structural classifications and lower bounds for $\lambda_{\min}(G)$, in particular underlying the description of graphs with smallest eigenvalue $\geq -1-\sqrt 2$.

Problem. Develop an analogous theory of signed Hoffman graphs for signed graphs. Concretely, define a notion of a signed Hoffman graph (with slim and fat parts and a sign function on its slim–slim and possibly slim–fat edges), define an associated special matrix and smallest eigenvalue, define a notion of $\mathcal F$-decomposition (or representation) of a signed graph by a family of signed Hoffman graphs, and establish the corresponding structure and reduction theorems. The theory should specialise to the classical Hoffman-graph theory when all signs are $+1$, and should be powerful enough to yield structural classifications and sharp lower bounds for $\lambda_{\min}(G,\sigma)$ for natural classes of signed graphs (for example, those with $\lambda_{\min}(G,\sigma)\geq -1-\sqrt 2$ or $\geq -2$).
artifact.category_tag: spectral graph theory of signed graphs
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made toward a Hoffman-graph theory for signed graphs. Greaves classified edge-signed graphs with smallest eigenvalue greater than -2; Abiad–Greaves–Koolen and others introduced signed analogues of line graphs; and a 2026 preprint develops a structure theory for signed graphs with fixed smallest eigenvalue (e.g. greater than -1-sqrt(2)). However, no single comprehensive analogue of the full Woo–Neumaier Hoffman-graph machinery for signed graphs has been established, so the program remains only partially carried out.

status_evidence.title: Signed analogue of line graphs and their smallest eigenvalues
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces signed analogues of line graphs and studies their smallest eigenvalues.
status_evidence.claim: Develops signed-graph counterparts of classical constructions used in Hoffman-graph theory.

status_evidence.title: A structure theory for signed graphs with fixed smallest eigenvalue
status_evidence.snippet: Structure theory for signed graphs with smallest eigenvalue at least λ, with applications to signed graphs with smallest eigenvalue greater than -1-sqrt(2).
status_evidence.claim: Recent paper builds substantial structure theory but does not present a complete signed Hoffman-graph framework.
